chunks: What al-Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me of, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from al-Washshāʾ, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀṣim, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about a man who does not find water, so he performs tayammum and stands in salat, then a servant comes and says, “Here is the water.” He said: “If he has not bowed in rukuʿ, then let him turn away and perform wudu (ablution). But if he has bowed, then let him continue in his salat.”

key_terms.فَلْيَنْصَرِفْ: let him leave and break off the prayer
key_terms.فَيَتَيَمَّمُ: he performs tayammum as a substitute purification
key_terms.يَرْكَعْ: he performs the bowing of rukuʿ

ai.seo_question: If someone begins salat with tayammum and then finds water during the prayer, should he stop or continue?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about one who begins salat with tayammum because water is unavailable, then finds water during the prayer. If water becomes available before rukuʿ, he should leave the prayer and perform wudu (ablution); if after rukuʿ, he should complete the prayer as he is.
